name: Motion Estimation Residual
description: Analyzes motion estimation residual energy — AI-generated motion creates distinctive residual patterns.
mechanism:
This method analyzes motion estimation residuals for video deepfake detection:

1. **Motion Estimation**: Dense optical flow is computed between consecutive frames using established algorithms (Farnebäck, Lucas-Kanade, or variational methods). This estimates per-pixel motion vectors describing the apparent motion field.

2. **Residual Computation**: The motion-compensated prediction is computed by warping frame t using the estimated flow to predict frame t+1. The residual R = I_{t+1} − W(I_t, flow) captures what the motion model couldn't predict — new content, disoccluded regions, and artifacts.

3. **Residual Distribution Analysis**: Natural video produces motion estimation residuals with characteristic distributions: small residuals in smooth regions (well-predicted), larger at occlusion boundaries and newly visible regions. The method analyzes residual statistics — AI-generated video may show anomalous residual patterns, particularly in face regions where generation artifacts create unpredictable inter-frame changes.

4. **Face-Background Residual Comparison**: The residual characteristics of face regions vs. background are compared. In authentic video, both regions show similar residual statistics (same camera motion, natural object motion). Deepfakes may produce elevated face residuals because the independently generated face doesn't follow physically consistent inter-frame motion.

5. **Temporal Residual Pattern Analysis**: The temporal signal of residual magnitude is tracked. Periodic or anomalous patterns — such as regular residual spikes at the generator's refresh rate or systematically higher face residuals — indicate deepfake manipulation. The score quantifies the deviation from expected motion estimation residual behavior.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
